A1.description: context in system turn, audio in user turn
A1.rule: the template's extra block is appended to the SYSTEM message (task_instruction)

A2.description: context in the user turn BEFORE the audio
A2.rule: the template's extra block is a USER-message text part placed before the audio part

A3.description: context in the user turn AFTER the audio
A3.rule: the template's extra block is a USER-message text part placed after the audio part

arrangements.note: T1 has no extra block, so all three of its arrangement cells render an IDENTICAL request -- a documented, harmless consequence of honoring the registered 4x3 grid literally, visible in 'renderings' below as three identical content_sha256 values per T1 slice.

X1.reason: AMI/NXT turn labels are meeting-invariant bare letters (confirmed before this manifest was built: every one of the four P-ATTR-smoke meetings' turn tables uses exactly the alphabet ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']), so swapping in a DIFFERENT meeting's roster would be a byte-for-byte no-op text change. Per the mission's own fallback instruction, X1 instead corrupts the turn-to-speaker-label mapping inside the slice metadata: a seeded fixed-point-free derangement of the label alphabet is applied to every slice's OWN roster (read off entry['turns']) before it is rendered into the context block, so the declared 'speakers in this excerpt' set is actually wrong relative to the audio -- a real corruption of the attribution channel.

T1.task_instruction:
You are transcribing and attributing one chunk of a multi-speaker meeting recording. Produce one line per speech segment in EXACTLY this format:
<speaker>|<text>
Use the KNOWN TERMS spelling and SPEAKER MAP roster names supplied below when confident; otherwise use the raw speaker cluster id from the CONTEXT section. Output ONLY these lines, one segment per line, with no extra commentary before, between, or after them.

T2.description: T1 + the SS0b deployment context block (meeting id, per-slice speaker roster read from the frozen manifest's own turn metadata, task framing)
T2.extra_block_rule: render_meeting_context_block(meeting_id, roster) -- varies per meeting/slice, see per_meeting_context below

T3.description: T2 + an explicitly EMPTY glossary slot (measures the slot's framing cost before any glossary supply exists)

T4.description: T2 + reinforced output-grammar section restating the grammar with a per-line format example
T4.reinforced_grammar_block:
=== OUTPUT FORMAT (reinforced) ===
Follow the <speaker>|<text> grammar exactly, one line per speech segment. Example of one valid line:
A|Let's get started with today's agenda.
Output nothing else: no headings, no blank lines, no commentary before, between, or after the lines.
